en: The Apadāna of the Elder Bhisamuḷāladāyaka Mandāravapupphiya Chapter 3.3 I gave a lotus-root to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher of the World. By that root-offering, I have attained this state of peace. (1) For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in heaven; Having enjoyed celestial pleasures, I was reborn among humans. (2) In every birth, I was always wealthy, prosperous, and possessed of great merit; I was handsome, fair-skinned, and endowed with all good qualities. (3) I was born into a family of great wealth, Possessing abundant grain and many cattle and horses. (4) I was honored by kings and ministers, And I was respected by the entire populace. (5) I was honored by those who were honored, And I was revered by those who were revered. (6) I was praised by those who were praised, And I was esteemed by those who were esteemed. (7) I was venerated by those who were venerated, And I was worshipped by those who were worshipped. (8) I was served by those who were served, And I was attended upon by those who were attended upon. “The Fully Awakened One named Phussa was one who had gone beyond all phenomena;
he was omniscient and desired solitude.”
having gained confidence in his mind toward that Conqueror of great compassion,
Having taken a lotus root and stalk,
I gave them to the Best of Buddhas.
Because I gave a lotus root at that time,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of the gift of the lotus root.
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Bhisamuḷāladāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Bhisamuḷāladāyaka.
